title: Herringbone Vinyl Plank: Cost and What to Know Before You Order
meta: Herringbone vinyl plank costs more in material and waste, not labor. Wills Flooring installs LVP for $2.50 per sq ft; here is a Sammamish ordering checklist.
keywords: herringbone vinyl plank cost, herringbone LVP installation, herringbone vinyl plank Sammamish, how much waste for herringbone flooring, chevron vs herringbone vinyl plank

blocks.lead: Herringbone vinyl plank costs more than a straight-lay floor mainly because of the material: herringbone-specific planks cost more per box, you order about 15 percent extra for waste instead of 10, and the layout needs a flatter subfloor. Wills Flooring's published vinyl plank labor rate is $2.50 per sq ft with a 500 sq ft minimum.
blocks.detail: On a 700 sq ft Sammamish entry and great room that means $1,750 in labor, plus the plank, underlayment and any prep we find at the free estimate. Read the ordering checklist before you buy a single box.

blocks.html: Herringbone has moved from Pinterest boards to real Sammamish entryways and kitchens over the last few years, and vinyl plank made it affordable. A common Reddit thread asks whether herringbone LVP is "just a gimmick that costs double." It is not, but it is a different product with different rules. Not every plank can be laid in herringbone, the subfloor has to be flatter, and the layout decisions happen before the first box is opened. Here is what we tell Pine Lake and Klahanie homeowners before they order.

blocks.text: What actually costs more with herringbone

items.title: Herringbone-specific planks
items.text: You cannot lay standard click-lock plank in herringbone. The pattern needs left and right planks with mirrored locking profiles, sold as A and B boxes. These lines cost more per square foot than the same brand's straight plank and there are fewer of them.

items.title: Waste goes from 10 to 15 percent
items.text: Every plank that meets a wall in a 45-degree pattern is cut, and the offcut rarely fits elsewhere. Rooms with lots of walls, closets and islands push waste higher. Order 15 percent over the measured area, and more for a small chopped-up space.

items.title: Flatter subfloor
items.text: Straight plank hides a gentle hump. Herringbone shows it as open joints at every angle change. We hold the subfloor to 1/8 in over 10 ft for herringbone, so leveling compound shows up on more quotes than it would for a straight lay.

items.title: Labor time, not labor rate
items.text: A herringbone floor takes roughly twice as long to lay because of the chalk-line setup, the border cuts and the A/B sequencing. Our published $2.50 rate still applies; on very small or complicated rooms we confirm labor at the free estimate rather than guess.

blocks.note: Chevron and herringbone are different products. A herringbone plank has square ends; a chevron plank is cut at an angle. Neither can be made from a standard plank on site.

blocks.text: What to know before you order

items.d: 1. Confirm it is a herringbone SKU
items.text: The box must say herringbone or list A and B planks. Ask the supplier for the layout guide; if there is none, it is not a herringbone product.
Measure the room to the foot, then add 15 percent. A 600 sq ft kitchen and entry needs about 690 sq ft of plank.
Short planks, around 24 in or less, read as classic parquet. Longer planks, 36 in or more, look modern and calm on a big Trossachs great room floor. Bring both sizes home.
A straight border plank around the room frames the pattern and hides the angled wall cuts. It uses more material and time, but it is the detail that makes herringbone look intentional.
We check flatness and moisture at the free visit. Many 1990s Sammamish plateau homes have OSB subfloors that have crowned slightly at joists; those get leveled before pattern work.

items.d: 6. Get all boxes from one lot
items.text: Color varies between dye lots, and herringbone puts every plank next to a plank from a different orientation. Mixed lots show up as a checkerboard.

blocks.text: Where herringbone works and where it does not

a.title: Do it when
items: It is one or two rooms you want to feature: entry, kitchen, dining
The room is roughly rectangular with few jogs
The subfloor is flat or you have budget to level it
You have chosen a herringbone-specific rigid-core plank

b.title: Reconsider when
items: You want it through the whole 2,400 sq ft house; the pattern becomes noise
The rooms are long and narrow hallways; the zigzag fights the space
The plank you love only comes in straight boxes
You are selling soon; a straight-lay neutral plank is the safer resale bet

blocks.html: One Sammamish-specific note. Big open-plan main floors in Klahanie and Sahalee often run from the entry straight through the kitchen to the family room with no doorways. A herringbone entry that stops at an arbitrary line in the middle of an open floor looks unfinished. Either run the pattern through the whole open area, or end it at a real threshold like a cased opening. We sketch this at the estimate so the transition lands where a direction change makes sense.

blocks.text: Mistakes that ruin a herringbone floor

items.html: Starting at a wall. Herringbone starts on a chalk line down the center of the room so the pattern is symmetrical at both walls. Starting in a corner sends the zigzag drifting.
Skipping the flatness check. Every angle joint is a place for a hump to show as a gap. Level first, always.
Ordering exactly 10 percent extra. You will run short at the last wall, and the reorder will be a different dye lot.
Choosing a thin flexible plank for a busy family. Sammamish households with kids and dogs need a rigid core and a 20 mil wear layer, in any pattern.
Ignoring expansion. A floating herringbone floor still needs its perimeter gap. South-facing plateau rooms warm up fast on a July afternoon and the floor moves.

blocks.text: Questions to ask before you sign

items: Is the plank a herringbone-specific SKU with A and B boxes, and does the installer have the layout guide?
How much waste is built into the material order, and is it from a single dye lot?
What flatness tolerance will the subfloor be held to, and is leveling a written line on the quote?
Where does the pattern start and where does it end, drawn on a sketch?
Is there a border, and what plank is used for it?
Is labor quoted per square foot with the total area written down?
What warranty covers the workmanship? At Wills Flooring it is one year on every installation.

faq.q: How much does herringbone vinyl plank cost to install?
faq.a: Wills Flooring's published vinyl plank labor is $2.50 per sq ft with a 500 sq ft minimum. Herringbone takes about twice as long to lay, and on small or complicated rooms we confirm labor at the free estimate. The bigger cost differences are the herringbone-specific plank and about 15 percent waste.

faq.q: Can regular vinyl plank be installed in a herringbone pattern?
faq.a: No. Standard click-lock planks lock in one direction and cannot meet at 90 degrees. Herringbone lines are sold with mirrored A and B planks. Glue-down plank can sometimes be cut and laid in herringbone, but the cut ends lose their factory bevel and the look suffers.

faq.q: How much extra should I order for herringbone?
faq.a: About 15 percent over the measured area for a simple rectangular room, and up to 20 percent for a kitchen with an island, a peninsula and several doorways. Order it all at once from one dye lot. Leftover boxes are worth keeping for future repairs.

faq.q: Is herringbone vinyl plank harder to keep clean?
faq.a: No. The surface is the same wear layer as a straight-lay plank from the same line, so sweeping and damp mopping are identical. The extra joints are locked and sealed the same way. Dirt does not collect in the pattern any more than in a straight floor.

faq.q: Does herringbone flooring add resale value in Sammamish?
faq.a: It makes an entry or kitchen memorable in listing photos, and buyers on the plateau respond to it in moderation. Running it through an entire house can polarize buyers. One or two feature rooms with a neutral tone is the safe version if resale is on your mind.

faq.q: Which rooms in a Sammamish home suit herringbone best?
faq.a: Entries, kitchens and dining rooms are the classics. In open plans, either run it through the whole connected space or stop at a cased opening. Long narrow hallways and small bedrooms usually look busier, not better, in herringbone.
